body:
Part of #2525 (slice 3 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

Depends on #2613 (CPU raster search) and #2158 (NFP placer).

## What to add

Research comment 2 of #2525 gives speed estimates from operation counts only. This issue measures them.

- Recorded part sets of 50, 200 and 1000 parts: rectangles, L shapes, parts with holes and parts with curves (as polylines). Make them in the test code from seeds, or keep them as small recorded files. Do not use a third-party benchmark file whose license is not clear.
- Rotation sets: locked, orthogonal (4), and 15-degree steps (24).
- For each set, measure in release: the run time of the NFP placer, the run time of the CPU raster search, the time for each part and rotation evaluation, the used sheet length and the material use in percent.
- Put the measurement in an `#[ignore]` heavy-lane test (its ignore reason names the lane). It must not run in the quick or batch gate.

## Decision

Write the numbers and a go or no-go for the GPU evaluator (#2525 slice 4) in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`. The rule: go when the evaluation step is more than half of the run time for 200 parts with orthogonal rotations, or for 15-degree steps. Comment the result on #2525's slice-4 issue.

## Notes

- No change to nest output. No MCP tool. No new dependency.
- Headless. No GPU.

## Done means

The heavy-lane test runs and prints the table. The decision entry has the table, the machine and the build profile, and the go or no-go for slice 4.
